lens.message:
Here's the shift: intelligence now splits, for us, into rented and owned. The substrate — models, compute, APIs — is interchangeable commodity; the perspective, individually held, is the asset we keep. Durable value sits on the owned side. That changes how we approach where we invest, how we make build-vs-rent calls on models and vendors, and what we count as our defensible asset.

The note, as written:

'Owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence.'
'The substrate is a commodity; the perspective is the asset you keep.'

Read through the shift, that's one claim about where value lives, not two aphorisms: anything rented can be swapped without losing what matters, because it's commodity. The perspective is the only part that compounds — the thing to own, keep, and invest in. Everything else, vendors included, is substrate. Even the note's own purpose fits: it exists so the positioning is something we hold and reuse, not something rebuilt from scratch each time.

Right lens?

On reach, honestly: this lands on one document — the positioning note itself. Nothing else is in view on this stream yet, so there's no wider list to apply it across. If the shift is right, the next documents that arrive get read through it.
